name: Axiom Systems Parasitic Data Harvester PDH-3
product_name: Axiom Systems Parasitic Data Harvester PDH-3
description: A device designed to be covertly attached to a target's neural interface charging cable, harvesting data from every charging session. The PDH-3 intercepts the data channel that neural interfaces use during charging to perform backup, update, and diagnostic operations, copying the transmitted data to an encrypted internal storage. Over successive charging sessions, the PDH-3 accumulates a comprehensive picture of the target's neural interface contents — communications, stored memories, access credentials, and cognitive enhancement configurations. The device is powered parasitically from the charging cable and adds no detectable load.

specifications.installation: Inline with neural interface charging cable
specifications.detectability: No additional load — transparent to diagnostics
specifications.retrieval: Physical removal or low-power burst transmission

story_hooks: A PDH-3 found on an executive's charging cable had been accumulating data for nine months — the stored data includes every credential, communication, and stored memory backup from that period.

PDH-3 devices have been found pre-installed in charging cables sold through a major retail chain — thousands of users may have been unknowingly sharing their neural interface data with an unknown collector.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, nearly imperceptible inline module disguised as a standard connector adapter. The form factor mimics legitimate charging cable components, with subtle ridging and recessed ports that allow it to blend seamlessly into a cable assembly. Its diminutive size makes it easily overlooked during casual inspection.
physical_description.dimensions: 10mm length × 5mm width × 3mm depth (smaller than a grain of rice when viewed end-on)
physical_description.weight_description: Negligible — less than 2 grams, adds imperceptible mass to charging cable
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened polymer composite shell with embedded graphene conduction layers; internal shielded circuit board
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with polished metallic connector contacts; surface etched with microscopic grip texture to prevent slipping during installation
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed silver connector pins; faint bioluminescent blue underlay visible only under direct UV
physical_description.interface_elements: Two recessed USB-C type connectors (male/female pass-through); minimal surface indicators — only a pinhole diagnostic LED (red/amber/green cycle) under the shell; micro SD extraction port concealed beneath adhesive label
distinctive_features: Pass-through design allows legitimate charging to continue uninterrupted
Connector pins aligned to minimize electromagnetic signature detection
Polymer housing has slight cable-matching texture variation to reduce tactile detection
Micro capacitor array creates zero load differential during charging diagnostics
Faint Axiom Systems serialization etched into underside in 0.5mm font
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Axiom Systems logo (Φ circuit symbol) laser-etched on undersurface; serial number and batch code in 0.3mm text; FCC-equivalent compliance marking for GLMZ Zone A (intentionally spoofed standard markings)
physical_description.condition_typical: Mounted inline on charging cable, partially obscured by cable management sleeves or routing clips; appears as minor cable thickening at connection point; shows minimal wear unless physically stressed during removal
